turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): in you go there, she's free. she was stuck at the computer.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): grand, thanks. sure this is hardly worth a visit.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): sit yourself down. sorry, uh the screen's after freezing again. one second. right, what's brought you in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): it's nothing. a bit of bloating and loose stools if I have milk or ice cream. been months. I'm grand apart from that.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): sorry, it beeped at me. say that once more?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): bloating, and the stools go loose. after milk, and after ice cream. err a few months now.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): any weight loss with it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): no. not a pound. if anything the jeans are...
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): hold on, wrong tab. what were you saying about the weight?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): no weight loss. same as always.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): any blood in the stool?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): fever? vomiting?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): no fever, no vomiting. it's minor.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): how often are the loose stools?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): umm not every day. only with the milk or the ice cream. a couple of times a week, if that.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): and the bloating, same time?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah, belly comes up a small bit, bit of wind, then it passes. nothing to write home about.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): did you try cutting the dairy?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I did a week with no milk and no ice cream. eased a small bit. then the weekend, I had the ice cream anyway.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): medicines, anything for the gut, or regular tablets?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): buscapan from the chemist, the ten milligram tablets, for the cramp. I stopped it in March, waste of time. uh the GP wrote immodium once and I never collected it.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): buscopan ten mg, stopped in March. and the loperamide you never took.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): never took it. no point.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): allergies to medicines or food?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): no. nothing.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): any conditions we treat you for?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): no. I'm healthy.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): surgery ever?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): no, never had an operation.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): and the family, diabetes, blood pressure, bowel problems?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, my brother is grand, another sister has pressure but no sugar, and there's no bowel problems in the family.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): sorry, an alert popped up. father had diabetes. say the sister again?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): sister has the pressure, high blood pressure, but no sugar. mother did not have the diabetes.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): work, hours, what you eat, exercise, drink, smoking?

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I work in the post office, hours are half eight till four Monday to Friday. diet is ordinary, meat and potatoes and a bit of dairy, that's the yoke of it, I walk the dog most evenings about twenty minutes, err a glass of wine at the weekend maybe two, and I never smoked.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): hours again? I was looking at the screen.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): half eight to four, five days.
[SEG0039] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): sorry doctor, lab's asking about the morning bloods, and I'm after being on to my own childminder, mad morning. are you sending bloods on this one?
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): give me two minutes and yes. pull the door after you.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): right, lie back and I'll feel the tummy. sore when I press?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): no. not sore at all.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): abdomen is soft, no tenderness, no mass. all quiet.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): right so. the lactose in the milk isn't broken down, it pulls water into the bowel, and that's the bloating and the loose stool. fits, near enough.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): so leave me off. it's only ice cream.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'd call it lactose intolerance for now. I can't rule out coeliac disease until the bloods are back.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I eat bread every day and I'm fine. it's the milk, not the bread.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): we'll still do a blood test for coeliac. stay on the gluten till it's done, or the test is a waste.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): fine. a lot of fuss, but fine.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): keep a diet diary for the next two weeks. food, and when the bloating or loose stools come.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): mm. a diary. I'll give it a go.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): come back in three weeks and we'll go through the diary and the result.
[SEG0053] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll book the coeliac bloods for Thursday morning and the review for three weeks. Thursday ok?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday's grand. thanks.

spec.situation: Person with bloating and loose stools after milk and ice cream for months, no weight loss; tried to avoid dairy for a week; blood test for coeliac planned; diet diary asked.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Imodium/loperamide was prescribed previously by GP but was never collected/never taken.
Buscopan 10 mg was bought from the chemist and was stopped in March because it was a waste of time/ineffective.
Loose stools are not daily; they occur only with milk or ice cream, a couple of times a week if that.
Bloating occurs at the same time as the milk-triggered episodes, with mild abdominal distension and wind, then passes.
No family history of bowel problems.
On abdominal exam, the abdomen was 'all quiet' (no abnormal bowel sounds noted).

omissions.text: Patient said Buscopan 10 mg was stopped in March because it was a waste of time.
GP had prescribed Imodium/loperamide once, but the patient never collected it and therefore never took it.
Loose stools occur only with milk or ice cream, a couple of times a week if that, and not every day.
Bloating is accompanied by abdominal wind and then passes; abdomen was not sore when pressed.
Avoiding milk and ice cream for one week only eased symptoms a small bit (partial improvement, not full relief).
No medication allergies and no food allergies were reported; the recorded allergy item is nonspecific and misses the explicit denial of food allergy as well as medicine allergy.
Family history also included that the brother is well.
Doctor advised the patient to come back in three weeks specifically to review both the diet diary and the coeliac blood test result.
